title: Data Center Developers Adapting As Tax Breaks Disappear
key_facts: Nearly a dozen states have paused or rolled back data center tax incentives in the past six months.

Between May and August, Maine, Minnesota and Nebraska repealed their breaks; Arizona, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Ohio paused programs; Pennsylvania, Delaware and North Carolina narrowed theirs.
The number of states offering incentives grew from 7 in 2009 to 38 by April.
Local governments, such as Fulton County, Georgia, are also rolling back tax abatements.
Panelists at Bisnow's Midwest conference said losing incentives hurts competitiveness but is not necessarily fatal; Microsoft's representative said power and land matter more.
Microsoft said in January it would no longer seek local property-tax reductions on new data centers.
quote_evidence: nearly a dozen states have paused or rolled back their data center tax incentives over the past six months.
“The tax incentives are not the core or the foundation that make or break the project,” said Abhijeet Shrivastava, program manager for global land development strategy at Microsoft.
why_it_matters_hint: The subsidy model that shaped where data centers were built is eroding.
notes: Industry-event reporting; speakers are industry insiders.
